plugins.name: VDL Mode 2 (EXPERIMENTAL)
plugins.author: FoxSDR project
plugins.summary: EXPERIMENTAL - never yet decoded a real aircraft. Decodes the VHF airband digital data link: ACARS messages and ground station announcements, from raw I/Q.
plugins.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: THIS HAS NEVER DECODED A SIGNAL FROM AN AEROPLANE. It was written from ICAO Annex 10 and the ETSI VDL Mode 2 standards, and tested only against a transmitter built from the same reading of them, so a green test shows the receiver and that transmitter agree with each other and says nothing about the air. Fifteen details of the signal could not be confirmed from any document; if one is wrong it decodes nothing, and that is the likely outcome until someone with a real recording corrects it. Do not rely on it for anything.

VDL Mode 2 is the digital data link airliners use in the VHF airband: 8-phase differential PSK at 10 500 symbols/s in 25 kHz channels, 136.975 MHz worldwide and a handful of regional channels between 136.1 and 136.975 MHz. This decodes it from raw I/Q at any receiver rate from 32 kS/s to 61.44 MS/s: the channel the receiver is tuned to and every channel of 136.700 to 136.975 MHz that falls inside the band, up to twelve at once, each as its own receiver. A rate of 1.024 MS/s or more centred on 136.8375 MHz covers all twelve.

It prints one line per frame: the frequency, who sent it and to whom (an aircraft's 24-bit ICAO address, a ground station's), and for an ACARS message the registration, label, block, message sequence number, flight and text. The ground stations' XID frames - including the announcement each sends about every two minutes - are decoded and named, with the parameters they carry: the station's own position, nearby airports, the frequencies to try. A message the error-correcting code mended is marked with how many octets it mended. A burst it cannot mend is refused and named, never shown in part; every frame is checked by its 16-bit frame check sequence. Every frame it recognises but does not decode is named with its length rather than dropped.

It brings an instrument window drawn as the flight-deck message printer, and a track source: the positions an XID frame states, each to a tenth of a degree, about 11 km, never guessed from a message's text.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it does not decode the controller-pilot data link (CPDLC), ADS-C or any other ATN message - they are named and their length given. It uses hard decisions only, so its sensitivity is that of the standard's basic receiver. It will not decode a carrier more than about 3.5 kHz off frequency, so a receiver that is not calibrated to about 20 ppm may miss everything. It plays no audio. It reassembles nothing: a message sent in several blocks is shown block by block.

Written clean-room from ICAO Annex 10 Volume III Chapter 6 and ETSI EN 301 841-1 and -2; no VDL Mode 2 decoder was read. Every constant is cited to its document and clause where it is defined.

Windows only so far: no Linux build exists, and the catalogue lists a Windows build alone.
plugins.legalNotice:
This plugin decodes third-party aircraft data link messages: the text airliners and their ground stations send each other, which can include operational, commercial and sometimes personal information. In the United Kingdom it is an offence under section 48 of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 to intercept a message you are not authorised to receive, or to disclose its contents. Comparable restrictions apply in many other jurisdictions, and some permit reception but prohibit disclosure or use.

This plugin is distributed separately from the application, and is not included in it, so that installing it is your informed decision. You are responsible for ensuring that your use of it is lawful where you are.

It is also EXPERIMENTAL and has never decoded a real signal. It is not a safety tool and must never be relied on for anything to do with the operation of an aircraft.

plugins.name: Demod Analyzer (EXPERIMENTAL)
plugins.author: FoxSDR project
plugins.summary: EXPERIMENTAL - works out what a digitally modulated signal is (BPSK, QPSK, 8PSK or 16-QAM) and measures it, live or from a recording; not yet tried against a real off-air signal.
plugins.description:
Reads a digitally modulated I/Q signal - the live receiver's VFO channel, or a recording it reads itself - and works out what it is: BPSK, QPSK, 8PSK or 16-QAM, with a confidence, chosen by which constellation the burst actually fits best rather than by the smallest error alone (which QPSK can win inside 8PSK or 16-QAM by cheating). Everything needed to get there is found automatically: the occupied band and the burst inside it, the symbol rate from the signal's own cyclostationary line, the carrier frequency, the raised-cosine roll-off, symbol timing and carrier phase, then EVM, MER, an SNR measured against the recording's own silence where there is one, timing and phase jitter, and I/Q gain and phase imbalance. Every recovered symbol becomes Gray-mapped bits - printable on the plate (PRINT BITS) or written whole, with every measurement, by EXPORT to a text file and a per-symbol CSV.

LIVE OR A FILE. Live, it reads the receiver's VFO channel exactly as set - whatever it is tuned and opened to - and re-analyses roughly twice a second. From a file, the path is typed into *I/Q file* in the plugin's settings, because the host gives plugins no file-open dialog: cs8 (HackRF `hackrf_transfer -r`), cu8 (RTL-SDR `rtl_sdr`), cs16, cf32 (GNU Radio `.cfile`), or WAV at 8/16/24/32-bit PCM or float. Everything else - forcing a modulation or symbol rate, a sync word to resolve the phase ambiguity, the matched filter, roll-off, sampling offset - is a setting with an automatic default that can be typed over.

ONE DASHBOARD PICTURE. The host gives a decoder exactly one image, so the constellation (density map with the ideal points and decision boundaries), the eye, the spectrum (carrier and occupied band marked), symbol power over the burst, and I/Q after the matched filter all share that one picture rather than a window each. The same numbers are also a panel table, and a line reaches Decoder output whenever the verdict changes.

EXPERIMENTAL - PUBLISHED WITHOUT EVER HAVING SEEN A REAL OFF-AIR SIGNAL. Every figure in the plugin's own notes is checked by `test_demodan` against a synthetic transmitter the test itself builds from the published constellation and Gray mappings, at several signal-to-noise ratios, on both Windows and Linux - never against a capture from a real modulator. The clearest way this can go wrong: a file read with the wrong sign convention - cs8 read as cu8, or the reverse - folds the constellation into something that still looks like a genuine, if noisy, 16-QAM (confidence 0.5-0.7, EVM around 25%); the EVM figure is the tell, not the verdict alone.

Asks for no permission beyond the ordinary decoder capabilities - it only ever reads the channel already open, and never asks to move the VFO. Needs FoxSDR 0.99.43+ for the settings form, plate keys and spectrum marks; an older host still gets the live picture and measurements with every setting at its default.

Written from the published estimators alone - Oerder & Meyr 1988 for symbol timing, Gardner 1986 for the tracking loop, Pauluzzi & Beaulieu 2000 for the M2M4 SNR estimate, Swami & Sadler 2000 for the classification cumulants - no other analyser's source was read.

plugins.name: Radiosondes (EXPERIMENTAL)
plugins.author: FoxSDR project
plugins.summary: EXPERIMENTAL - the block CRC and Reed-Solomon layout have not yet been confirmed on frames from a real flight, so it may decode nothing until then. Follows Vaisala RS41 weather-balloon sondes on 400-406 MHz: serial, position, height, climb rate and wind.
plugins.description:
Decodes the Vaisala RS41 radiosonde, the weather balloon's transmitter, on 400-406 MHz. Given raw I/Q from a Radio (2.4 MS/s suggested; any rate from about 20 kS/s works), it searches the capture for carriers itself, because a sonde's frequency is set at the launch site and nobody tells you, and follows them as they drift. For each sonde it reports the serial number, position, height, climb rate and wind, and draws its trail on the map as a balloon silhouette. Up to four sondes are followed at once, anywhere in the capture. Three presets cover the band: 400-402, 402-404 and 404-406 MHz. On the patch page, wire it to a Radio to search the whole capture, or to a Channel for the one sonde in it, and its map output into a Map.

EXPERIMENTAL - PUBLISHED WITHOUT EVER HAVING SEEN A REAL FLIGHT. The frame format was written from a published protocol description (bazjo/RS41_Decoding's, plus Vaisala's own datasheet; no decoder's source was read) and is checked by the plugin's own test against frames the test builds itself. Two choices the description leaves open have not been confirmed on frames from a real flight: which CRC-16 variant covers each block, and how the 48 parity bytes and the data are split between the two Reed-Solomon codewords. The test's frames share those choices, so it cannot catch a wrong one. If either is wrong the plugin will report no sondes at all, so it may decode nothing until someone checks it against a real RS41.

What it does not do: no temperature, humidity or pressure (the calibration maths for them has no usable published description), no landing prediction, and no sonde other than the RS41.

It was asked for through the app's feature-request box on 2026-10-02, for weather-balloon tracking.

Windows only so far: no Linux build exists yet, and the store offers no Linux download of this plugin until one is published.
